correctness.rationale: With the convention A(a,b)=⟨g,M_bT_ag⟩, for a≠0 the exact expansion is ω^-a³[sum_j ω^{-3aj²+(3a²+b)j}+t(1+ω^{ab})]/K. The quadratic Gauss evaluation gives ε_pχ_p(-3a)√p ω^{(3a²+b)²/(12a)} with ε_p=1 or i depending on p mod4. Writing 1+ω^{ab}=2C ω^r, r=ab/2 mod p, forces for p≡3 mod4 an imaginary iω^E unable to be real (odd p), and for p≡1 mod4 the congruence E=(9a⁴+b²)/(12a)=0 plus strict χ(-3a)C<0, with unique t=√p/(2|C|). At a=0, normalized ambiguity is 1 (b=0) or t(t+2)/K>0 (b≠0). Independent modular enumeration p=5,13,17,29,37 reproduced 0,0,8,16,36 candidate zero pairs; p=17 shows exactly two distinct amplitudes with four pairs each and direct complex ambiguity sums vanish at their corresponding locations. The Fourier diagonalization of the p² Gabor projector Gram matrix has eigenvalues proportional to |A(a,b)|², so exactly four zero coefficients give linear tomography rank p²−4. Zero ambiguity is NOT claimed to exclude rank-one phase retrieval. The all-prime result is the Gauss identity/phase reasoning, not finite floating comparisons.
